concepts.title: Fracture Nexus — Hero Overview
concepts.design_question: What does the entire game mean by dimensions?
concepts.prompt:
Create a Roblox-native environment concept for GRAB THE WEIRD. It must look buildable inside Roblox Studio: blocky Roblox-scale figures, chunky simplified geometry, toy-like polished materials, clean silhouettes, readable colors, clear floors and restrained lighting. Use the supplied reference only for proportion, palette, readable silhouettes and cyan Rift language; do not reproduce their characters, branding text or exact composition. No photorealism, Unreal Engine realism, Pixar or Fortnite anatomy, generic fantasy filigree, surface micro-detail, excessive bloom, arbitrary neon or purposeless floating debris. Every impossible feature must explain a gameplay rule. No captions, UI, logos or watermarks. Show actual level-design logic rather than atmosphere alone. Violet and magenta are confined to dimensional fracture seams; cyan remains the clearest stable-travel cue. Compose one coherent environment view, not a collage or promotional board; only the artifact study uses an object sheet.

PRIMARY DESIGN SUBJECT: A fractured research crossing around one central Dimensional Core. Giant's Kitchen counters form the warm left cluster; a broken Moon Aquarium dome forms the cool right cluster; chunky Toybox rails form the upper cluster; an upside-down city is a distant silhouette. Each cluster connects to the Core by a visible broad bridge.
GAMEPLAY READ: Three blocky players carry one large golden refrigerator together toward a visible cyan return gate. Show an optional side loop without hiding the safe route.
DIMENSIONAL RULE: Each fragment retains its own local gravity, but all usable bridge decks share a stable orientation. Orbiting architecture is a distant landmark outside the carry path.
LANDMARK: One faceted split Core supported above the central platform, visible from every approach.
TRAVERSAL: Clear ground-level cargo route, broad straight bridges, generous turning pads, a short ramp and portal windows framing possible future dimensions.
PLAYER SCALE: Recognizable blocky Roblox figures, consistent limb proportions and solid foot contact; no exact character cloning.
ARTIFACT: One chunky golden refrigerator with a single cyan eye; legible against the neutral floor.
COLOR LANGUAGE: Ink-blue Core framing; cream/wood/coral Kitchen; deep navy/pale aqua Aquarium; muted primary Toybox colors; gold artifacts and cyan travel only.
CAMERA: Wide elevated 24mm view that exposes all bridges, arrival and return route; keep the distant city subordinate.

review.observations: A dark faceted Core sits on a round central platform. Warm Kitchen counters approach from the left, a broken blue Aquarium dome from the right, a raised toy/train cluster behind, and an inverted city stays in the distance. Three blocky figures move a gold refrigerator along a broad foreground bridge. The route-to-landmark composition is clear.
review.required_corrections: Prune most unrelated background floating cubes; do not turn decorative city silhouettes into false playable routes. Simplify Core detail and prove all three bridge junctions and cargo turns.

concepts.design_question: How do two dimensions physically bleed into each other?
concepts.prompt:

Compose one coherent environment view, not a collage or promotional board; only the artifact study uses an object sheet.

PRIMARY DESIGN SUBJECT: An oversized kitchen counter enters a cracked orbital Aquarium wall. A single spherical volume of water hangs across the ceiling; the top half of a chunky refrigerator intersects the water while its base stays on the floor. Stars are visible through one bounded wall opening.
GAMEPLAY READ: Three blocky players steer a large Moon-in-a-Jar along a dry lower route. One player investigates a raised side catwalk.
DIMENSIONAL RULE: Suspended water changes gravity for loose utensils above the catwalk; the dry cargo route stays stable. A utensil's motion follows this one visible volume rather than random levitation.
LANDMARK: Half-submerged refrigerator and one large water sphere share the crossover seam.
TRAVERSAL: A broad dry route curves around the sphere's support, with turning space, a gentle ramp and a raised optional catwalk. Both exits are visible.
PLAYER SCALE: Recognizable blocky Roblox figures, consistent limb proportions and solid foot contact; no exact character cloning.
ARTIFACT: A chunky transparent jar with a solid small moon and a simple gold handle.
COLOR LANGUAGE: Cream/coral kitchen surfaces transition to navy/pale aqua through one clean seam; cyan remains reserved for gates.
CAMERA: Wide 24mm corner view exposing entry, both route heights and the exit; show the water boundary clearly.

review.observations: One spherical water volume intersects the upper refrigerator and ceiling. Warm kitchen surfaces and blue Aquarium masonry share the same room. Loose utensils sit inside the water volume; a raised catwalk passes behind the fridge. A continuous dry floor and a visible right-hand ramp support the carry route.
review.required_corrections: Do not copy the centre fridge into the validated straight lanes. Simplify stacked glass/water; retain one sphere visual and one behavior volume. The right ramp must be cargo-rated only after physical testing.

PRIMARY DESIGN SUBJECT: An enormous faceted dimensional reactor split into three readable shell pieces. Architectural fragments orbit inside a contained central shaft. Two levels of chunky catwalks frame the reactor.
GAMEPLAY READ: Four blocky players regroup on a broad lower landing, with one carrying a heavy artifact. An upper route shows a tempting pickup.
DIMENSIONAL RULE: The Core's orbit is confined to the shaft; the lower return deck stays stable. Broken upper platforms explain the optional hazard.
LANDMARK: A three-piece fractured reactor with a visible solid centre and asymmetric gold clamps.
TRAVERSAL: An uninterrupted lower cargo loop, two wide turning landings and a side ramp to the optional upper level; do not place a jump on the mandatory carry route.
PLAYER SCALE: Recognizable blocky Roblox figures, consistent limb proportions and solid foot contact; no exact character cloning.
ARTIFACT: A large clockwork jellyfish on the optional landing with a bell-shaped block shell and a few simple rods.
COLOR LANGUAGE: Ink/navy structural frame, warm cream walkways, restrained gold clamps, one cyan return portal.
CAMERA: Wide 20–24mm view from a lower corner showing vertical scale, stable loop and both landings.

review.observations: The result uses two opposed reactor caps around a faceted blue centre rather than the proposed three shell pieces. Lower walkways surround the landmark; a side ramp reaches an upper route and the jellyfish reward sits on a separate elevated landing. The central negative space communicates vertical scale.
review.required_corrections: Reject the image's pervasive pillar glow and cyan-Core/travel ambiguity for the production palette. Do not infer a safe upper jump or cargo access from the floating reward landing.

PRIMARY DESIGN SUBJECT: A dark, almost empty dimensional shaft with one clear out-and-back bridge to a rare artifact. Two distant portal windows reveal unrelated realities but remain background silhouettes.
GAMEPLAY READ: Two blocky players pause at a safe landing and judge the one dangerous route. A third has turned back toward a visible return doorway.
DIMENSIONAL RULE: A single moving gap interrupts the optional bridge on a readable cycle; the entry landing remains stable.
LANDMARK: A rare Small Sun suspended above a simple pedestal at the far landing.
TRAVERSAL: One broad optional route with a clearly visible hazard gap, safe waiting pads on either side and a return path in frame.
PLAYER SCALE: Recognizable blocky Roblox figures, consistent limb proportions and solid foot contact; no exact character cloning.
ARTIFACT: A solid faceted Small Sun in a compact cage; bright enough to attract the eye without bloom filling the scene.
COLOR LANGUAGE: Matte navy/black void, pale grey bridge edges, a controlled amber artifact focal point, cyan only at the return door.
CAMERA: Wide 28mm view behind the deciding players, showing the entire risk and destination without hiding the way back.

review.observations: Two figures consider a single bridge toward a caged Small Sun. A third turns toward the cyan return gate on the left. The dark void, bright destination and visible interrupted bridge make the optional risk clear; two framed background realities remain separated from the usable route.
review.required_corrections: Do not copy impossible disconnected rail/collision segments as authored geometry. The waiting-pad safety and gap timing need real tests; avoid adding another competing anomaly.

PRIMARY DESIGN SUBJECT: A Kitchen/Aquarium crossover collapses behind three blocky players carrying one bulky artifact. One emergency extraction gate is ahead, framed by solid dark supports. A bounded water anomaly moves beside the failing secondary route.
GAMEPLAY READ: Players retreat together along a broad visible path to the emergency gate. One losing route is clearly behind them, with another continuous route still available.
DIMENSIONAL RULE: Collapse progresses from the rear toward the gate; an alternate return deck stays intact long enough for cargo. Water drift is side pressure, not random full-screen chaos.
LANDMARK: The emergency cyan gate, visible through the entire foreground route.
TRAVERSAL: Continuous cargo-width floor and turning landing, one collapsing branch in the background, a readable surviving bypass. Show the end of the path.
PLAYER SCALE: Recognizable blocky Roblox figures, consistent limb proportions and solid foot contact; no exact character cloning.
ARTIFACT: One oversized gold refrigerator held by the group; do not obscure their feet or the gate.
COLOR LANGUAGE: Warm cream/wood foreground; dark navy collapsing background; local amber warnings; cyan return gate remains the clearest focal point.
CAMERA: Wide 24mm side-rear view exposing feet, cargo, bypass and gate; frozen final 20–40-second design keyframe.

review.observations: Three blocky figures carry the refrigerator on a wide warm deck toward a large cyan extraction frame. The side/upper route visibly breaks apart behind them while water remains below the safe deck. Feet, floor and destination are all readable.
review.required_corrections: Do not treat rendered arrows as sufficient navigation or copy side-route destruction into the only cargo path. The still image does not establish high-intensity motion, timing or server-safe topology change.

PRIMARY DESIGN SUBJECT: An almost empty impossible ivory/black void with a single solid platform, one strange artifact and three distant framed doorways into unrelated dimensions.
GAMEPLAY READ: Two blocky players stand still near a quiet pedestal; a third waits by the obvious return doorway.
DIMENSIONAL RULE: Background doorways reveal remote realities but do not imply walkable floating stepping stones. The one real floor remains contiguous.
LANDMARK: A lone Runaway Door artifact standing at a slight impossible angle on a quiet pedestal.
TRAVERSAL: A broad uninterrupted floor, a wide turn around the pedestal and one usable return doorway connected to the same floor.
PLAYER SCALE: Recognizable blocky Roblox figures, consistent limb proportions and solid foot contact; no exact character cloning.
ARTIFACT: One blocky freestanding door with two small wheel-like feet and a simple handle; strong silhouette.
COLOR LANGUAGE: Ivory floor, near-black background, restrained ink frames and a single gold artifact detail; cyan only at the active return.
CAMERA: Wide 28mm composition with deliberate negative space, artifact isolated and both player scale and return route readable.

review.observations: A plain ivory platform surrounds one raised wheeled-door pedestal. Three distant framed views into unrelated worlds contrast with one cyan return doorway. Two figures contemplate the artifact and one waits at the return. Quiet negative space creates rarity without chaos.
review.required_corrections: Do not make every background frame look equally usable. No physics behavior or drop-recovery guarantee can be inferred from the wheeled pedestal pose.

PRIMARY DESIGN SUBJECT: A stable research plaza with one huge primary Rift gate, a simple physical Dimensional Atlas showing three discovered nodes, and a visible museum/research wing.
GAMEPLAY READ: Three blocky players return with one large artifact and move toward a visible display bay. Another player studies the Atlas from a clear side area.
DIMENSIONAL RULE: Home stabilises impossible artifacts inside bounded display spaces. The Atlas shows discoveries without changing the main return floor.
LANDMARK: One primary cyan gate in a dark chunky frame, paired with a restrained orbit diagram.
TRAVERSAL: The spawn faces the portal. A clear broad route leads from arrival to the museum; Atlas viewers cannot block the entry/join approach.
PLAYER SCALE: Recognizable blocky Roblox figures, consistent limb proportions and solid foot contact; no exact character cloning.
ARTIFACT: A recovered Moon-in-a-Jar held by two players near a simple plinth.
COLOR LANGUAGE: Warm cream and wood, ink research structures, gold progress accents and cyan travel. Calm directional lighting contrasts with fractured rooms.
CAMERA: Wide 24mm view from the spawn approach, showing return gate, museum destination and Atlas side station.

review.observations: The primary gate dominates the left approach. A museum/research facade gives a visible home destination, while a three-node Atlas occupies a side plinth. Two figures bring a jar artifact toward the plaza. The museum entrance is reached by stairs, so the image does not supply a proven heavy-cargo route into the gallery.
review.required_corrections: Add reliable cargo access to the museum before accepting the layout. Remove unnecessary floating backdrop pieces and avoid presenting three Atlas nodes as already functional progression.

concepts.title: Hybrid Artifact Sheet
concepts.design_question: How do artifacts show their dimensional history?
concepts.prompt:
Create a Roblox-native environment concept for GRAB THE WEIRD. It must look buildable inside Roblox Studio: blocky Roblox-scale figures, chunky simplified geometry, toy-like polished materials, clean silhouettes, readable colors, clear floors and restrained lighting. Every impossible feature must explain a gameplay rule. No captions, UI, logos or watermarks. Show actual level-design logic rather than atmosphere alone. Violet and magenta are confined to dimensional fracture seams; cyan remains the clearest stable-travel cue. Compose one coherent environment view, not a collage or promotional board; only the artifact study uses an object sheet.

PRIMARY DESIGN SUBJECT: A clean seven-object concept sheet: Clockwork Jellyfish, Moon in a Jar, Bottomless Frozen Cup, Orbiting Golden Fridge, Runaway Door, Small Sun, Reverse Fishbowl. Each is a chunky Roblox-buildable assembly with no tiny filigree.
GAMEPLAY READ: Use three small blocky Roblox figures as a shared scale key along the bottom, without making this a character poster. Objects must look graspable or cooperative to carry.
DIMENSIONAL RULE: Each object's silhouette implies one behavior: jellyfish pulses, jar contains a moon, cup has impossible depth, fridge has a bounded orbit, door moves away, sun glows locally, fishbowl reverses inside and outside.
LANDMARK: Seven distinctly different silhouette families with three to five large visible pieces each.
TRAVERSAL: Use front three-quarter object views with clear bounding boxes and uncluttered negative space; show no environment or cosmetic levitation unrelated to the behavior.
PLAYER SCALE: Recognizable blocky Roblox figures, consistent limb proportions and solid foot contact; no exact character cloning.
ARTIFACT: All seven named objects; do not add duplicates or an eighth item.
COLOR LANGUAGE: Limited cream/ink/steel bases; restrained dimension color; gold fridge and sun; aqua only for water-like contents and cyan eye.
CAMERA: Orthographic-like wide artifact sheet, 4:3 aspect ratio; no perspective trick that hides contact points.

review.observations: The sheet contains all seven requested names and distinct large-piece silhouette families. The jellyfish uses a bell and repeated mechanical limbs; jar/cup/bowl use contained volumes; fridge uses a bounded orbit; Small Sun is faceted. Tiny figures and blank ruler marks at the bottom do not establish reliable object dimensions. The sheet's Runaway Door lacks the wheeled feet shown in F.
review.required_corrections: Reject unlabelled ruler ticks as measurements and exclude text labels from runtime assets. Add explicit contact geometry; the reverse fishbowl behavior and cooperative fridge carry are unproved by a static sheet.
